# Changelog

**This changelog is maintained automatically** — a scheduled workflow (`.github/workflows/daily-changelog.yml`) summarizes each day's merged PRs into a dated entry and commits it on its own; do not edit this file by hand. Archie ships continuously, so changes are grouped by the **date they landed** on `main` rather than by version. Each entry leads with the **value** it delivers, then adds **technical detail**; pure plumbing stays technical. The [starting-point snapshot](#before-this-log--the-starting-point) at the bottom is where Archie stood before the first entry.

## 2026-08-20

- **The PM no longer barges into conversations meant for someone else, and no longer publishes a conclusion while its own dispatched research is still outstanding.** It used to wake on any reply in a thread it was working — mention, bare name, or neither — and post a full reply whenever it had a correction to make, even when the message asked it nothing; separately, it would publish a full verdict while a question it had delegated was still unanswered, then post a correction minutes later once the real answer landed, in one case after a named person had already spent time replying to a question that was withdrawn shortly after. Both now reduce to one test each: silence unless some part of the message actually asks the PM something, and no conclusion while a dispatched request on that question is still open — a one-line status update instead. _Technical: prompt-only change across `prompts/pm-agent.md` and `src/agents/prompts.ts`, refined over three commits into a single collapsed rule rather than a growing list of special cases; typecheck clean, 1462 tests passing (nothing asserts on prompt copy, so expected inert). PR #301._

## 2026-08-19

- **A trigger-fired task now stays in the conversation it started, instead of a human's reply to it opening a brand-new, context-free task.** A channel-message trigger used to tell the PM only that "a new message matched your filter" without ever passing along what was actually said, and a scheduled trigger posted its result with a detached tool that linked to nothing — so a reply from a human landed in a stranger task with no history and no access to the trigger's own working directory. A message fire now ingests the triggering thread through the same path every other Slack task uses, and a schedule fire opens and owns a thread in its bound channel from its very first post, so every later reply keeps routing back to the run that started it. _Technical: `fireTrigger` calls `task.append(thread)` for message fires and sets `metadata.home_channel` for schedule fires, both flowing through the single Slack render path from #291; the home channel counts as the task's own for canvas briefs, pinned messages, `list_channels` and file allowlists; a canvas-suppression mechanism was built to avoid a stray notice ahead of a fire's result, then reverted after live QA showed the notice wasn't actually a preamble; verified live against the real Slack workspace across four scenarios plus 1463 passing tests. PR #298._
- **Archie's git and GitHub credit finally resolves to a real, mentionable account, and every PR it opens now states who it was opened for.** Commit co-author trailers had silently credited nobody since the account address was built from Archie's numeric app ID rather than its actual user ID — GitHub matches that address by ID and drops the credit on any mismatch rather than falling back to the name — and a PR's true human owner was previously left to the model to mention in prose, or not at all, recoverable only by opening a commit and checking its author. `create_pull_request` now stamps a prominent "Opened by @archie-hq on behalf of &lt;name&gt;" note on every PR it creates. _Technical: new `getArchieAttributionIdentity()` (from `ARCHIE_GITHUB_LOGIN`/`ARCHIE_GITHUB_USER_ID`/`ARCHIE_GITHUB_NAME`) separates the credited identity from the app identity used to authenticate; falls back to the app bot unset or on a non-numeric id; measured on a real PR (archie-plugins#168). PR #295._
- **Slack messages that arrive as attachment cards, tables, or bot alerts — a Grafana alert, a Bugsnag error, a webhook report — no longer reach Archie as a blank line.** Three of seven places that turned a Slack payload into agent-readable text were still reading a field documented as holding only "the author's own typed text", silently dropping everything else a message carried; a narrow three-entry allowlist for inbound message subtypes also meant Slack's other ~30 subtypes, including plain bot posts, were dropped with no warning. Both are replaced with one shared render path and a deny-only list that forwards anything not explicitly excluded. _Technical: `message-body.ts` is now the sole render module (`text` renamed `ownText` throughout so a mis-read can't compile); `shouldForwardMessageEvent` split into `mayWakeTask`/`mayReachTriggers` over a shared 17-entry denylist; verified live against the real workspace plus 1409 passing tests. PR #291._
- **A sandboxed agent's shell can now actually read the core skill files it has loaded, closing a gap where that access silently depended on an accidental route rather than a real grant.** `buildSandboxConfig` denied all of `/app`, including `skills/`, with nothing re-allowing it, so a direct file read failed — the one path that appeared to work did so only because a workspace symlink slipped past the guard's unresolved-path check, not because access was actually granted. _Technical: `coreSkillPaths()` grants only the skills an agent actually mounts, added to `allowReadPaths` on both the base and repo spawn tracks; measured in-container under `bwrap` 0.11.0 across three access patterns; loading a skill via the `Skill` tool was never affected, since it reads in-process and was never gated by this guard. PR #290._
- _Technical: the `archie-e2e` skill's setup docs now explain why linking main's whole `workdir/` (not just recreating one) matters — `workdir/plugins` is itself a symlink to a local `archie-plugins` checkout, so a worktree that builds its own `workdir/` boots healthy with zero agents registered and no error, a failure mode that previously cost a full diagnostic cycle to trace. PR #294._

## 2026-08-18

- **Triggers — Archie's scheduled automations — can now leave notes for their own future fires instead of quietly redoing the same work forever.** Every fire used to spawn a brand-new task with no writable storage that survived it, so a trigger meant to build on its own history ("summarize what changed since last time", "chase up what you flagged yesterday") had nowhere to put anything and silently repeated itself instead — the kind of failure that looks like it's working. Each trigger now gets one directory that persists across fires, granted read-write to every agent on a trigger-fired task and paired with a new `trigger-task` skill that teaches the conventions (treat existing contents as data, prefer appending, prune your own entries) without prescribing any file structure. _Technical: directory created idempotently at agent spawn (not at fire) keyed off the persisted `triggered_by` metadata, gated on the trigger record still existing so a deleted trigger's directory can't be resurrected by a later spawn; removed through the single existing `deleteTrigger` chokepoint so all seven deletion entry points inherit it for free; granted in both sandbox read and write lists after live measurement under bwrap 0.11.0 disproved a documented "read grant clobbers write grant" limitation that had shaped an earlier write-only design — and had itself caused a live failure, since the agent was told the shell couldn't reach the directory and gave up instead of trying `ls`; verified live end-to-end (fire 2 read fire 1's file with no filename in its prompt) plus 18 acceptance criteria audited blind; 82 files / 1152 tests passing. PR #286._

## 2026-08-17

- **Archie stopped talking over reviewers on their own PRs — GitHub review comments, review bodies, and CI results now go to the agent who owns the branch instead of being narrated back into the Slack thread.** A reviewer left inline comments on eight backend PRs and Archie replied to every one in Slack, including relaying the reviewer's own words back at them and asking what one of their comments meant; the reviewer had to say outright "let's discuss only on the PRs, stop adding review-related replies here." The prompt's premise — "the user exists only in the channel" — is corrected at the source rather than patched with a rule that argues with it. _Technical: GitHub webhook wake prompts split into `githubInput` (review comments/bodies, PR conversation, CI results — routed to the branch owner) versus `existingTask` (merge outcomes only, still PM's to announce); a stale docstring claiming PM inspects checks with `get_pr_checks` corrected. PR #284._
- **Package installs (`npm`/`yarn`) now share one cache across every task instead of each task keeping its own copy, cutting sandbox disk growth from roughly 18 GB/day to about 1 GB/day and making repeat installs near-instant.** Measured on prod before the fix: 697 per-task caches holding ~285 GB, none of it ever reclaimed since nothing deletes a finished task's directory; a second task installing the same lockfile now reuses the shared cache in seconds instead of re-downloading it. _Technical: caches moved from `<task>/agents/<agent>/.cache` to a single `workdir/caches/`, safe to share because npm/Yarn Berry verify cache content against lockfile integrity hashes on read; `_npx`'s materialized, unverified `node_modules` is an accepted exception, documented at the call site; live verification on a booted instance caught and fixed a real regression where the E2E egress probe's own sandbox wasn't allow-listed for the new shared path. PR #283._
- _Technical: unified how archie-hq's own core skills are mounted onto agents behind one ordered `skillPaths` list and a central `CORE_SKILL_MOUNTS` manifest, replacing two separate fields whose implicit directory-based wiring made adding a skill's audience require a new field; behavior is unchanged (all four core skills stay PM-only), and a boot warning now names any core skill no agent track mounts. PR #281._
- _Technical: `workdir` and `claude-data` were tracked in `main` as self-referential symlinks (a `.gitignore` pattern with a trailing slash doesn't match the symlink form), so every checkout recreated a broken link that failed `docker compose up` and the `archie-e2e` harness; both entries are untracked and the ignore patterns widened to cover the symlink form too. PR #285._

## 2026-08-09

- **Archie now reads a channel's pinned messages, not just its canvas brief — so a runbook or decision pinned two years ago and still lived by doesn't get lost.** Every agent spawned for a task now sees a one-line index of what a channel pinned, newest first, with both pin and message dates/ages so an old pin can be weighed against a fresh one instead of being filtered out; the PM can open any individual pin the same way it opens a canvas file, and pins from external or unclassifiable people are excluded. Verified live against the real Sweatcoin workspace after granting the new `pins:read` scope, which surfaced and fixed four defects unit tests had all passed: bot-posted pins (including Archie's own, pinned by a human) were being wrongly refused, a JSON-bodied pin leaked its raw wrapper into the summary, and pins made minutes earlier were reported as pinned "yesterday". _Technical: `ensureChannelPins` scans off the same TTL-bounded hooks as the canvas, gated on both the pinned item's author and its pinner classifying as internal; summaries are cached by a digest of the source text (verbatim under 200 characters, one Haiku call above it, capped at six model calls per scan); pinned content is escaped (not stripped) against forging its own container tags, hardened over three rounds of adversarial QA; ships dormant in any workspace until `pins:read` is granted and the app reinstalled. 78 files, 1108 tests. PR #269._
- _Technical: documents how to prepare a git worktree for the E2E boot harness — `workdir`/`claude-data` must stay symlinked (shared, not copied, since the harness expects concurrent container access) while `secrets/` must be a real copy, because Docker's build context doesn't follow symlinks at the root the way bind mounts do. PR #271._

## 2026-08-08

- **Archie no longer drops message content Slack ships in shapes it doesn't parse — pasted Jira links, attachment cards, tables, and bot alerts now reach the agent instead of vanishing.** A user linked a Jira ticket in a DM and Archie insisted three times that no link had arrived; the chip's shape (`attachment_mention`) fell through an allowlisted switch and left a blank line where the link had been. Measured against 3,778 real messages across 11 channels, the same gap ate alert names and dashboard links (57 of 60 #mobile-alerts messages carry no text at all outside the card), whole tables, release-bot headlines, GitHub PR previews, and newest thread replies past the first page. A new backstop diffs rendered output against the raw payload and flags anything unaccounted for, catching three of these shapes that manual review had missed; edited messages and the explore read tools (`read_channel_history`, `read_thread`) now go through the same extraction as everything else. _Technical: `attachment_mention`/`message_mention`/`table`/`card`/`markdown`/`image`/`video`/`actions`/`divider` block cases added; text reconciled line-wise to avoid whole-body duplication; thread fetch paginates; `collectUnrenderedText` backstop degrades to "found nothing" on its own exceptions rather than risking ingestion; Slack Connect redaction verified end-to-end against real guest-authored payloads (183/183 redacted, 0 leaks); residue over the corpus reduced to 0; 1030 tests passing, verified live against production Slack traffic. PR #266._
- **A user @mentioning Archie for a brand-new task could get no reply at all — the PM sometimes read the trigger as an empty system event and silently ended its turn.** Every other trigger string tells the PM to check `knowledge.log` for the actual request; the new-task trigger was the one exception, reading as a contentless bootstrap message, which one live run's own reasoning treated as license to skip reading the log and report completion in silence. _Technical: `newTask` trigger string in `AGENT_PROMPTS` now names `knowledge.log`, matching its five siblings — a prompt nudge, not a structural guard, since the failure was a roughly one-in-six nondeterministic short-circuit rather than a broken code path. PR #267._

## 2026-08-07

- **Archie's core skills — including the ones that govern posting into other channels and setting up automations — have been silently unloadable in any deployed instance since the day each was introduced; now fixed.** `skills/` was never copied into the production Docker image or mounted in dev compose, so every `Skill` call for `self-awareness`, `channel-canvas`, `triggers`, or `thread-conduct` failed with "Unknown skill" — caught live when the PM tried loading `thread-conduct` twice, got errors both times, and posted into another channel with none of that guidance. _Technical: `COPY skills/` added to `Dockerfile.prod`, `./skills:/app/skills` mounted in `docker-compose.yml`, mirroring how `prompts/` is already handled. PR #262._
- **Archie now posts noticeably less to Slack, and tailors what it says to who's actually reading.** Three days of production traffic showed an 8.6:1 agent-to-human word ratio and 79% of consecutive posts separated only by an inbound agent report, so the old one-adjective "keep it brief" guidance is replaced with rules to answer only what was asked and post conclusions instead of running commentary; separately, the PM now sees a roster of the humans in the task with their Slack profile job titles, so it can write for an actual audience instead of defaulting to a technical one. _Technical: `<people_in_task>` block built from already-cached `profile.title`, withheld from external/guest users and sanitized against prompt injection; 20 new tests. PR #261._
- **Archie now reads a destination channel's own house rules before posting into it, not just the rules of the channel it's replying from.** Escalating into another channel — or replying in a cross-linked thread — used to carry only the origin channel's context, so a destination's own conventions (who to tag, how to phrase things) had no way to reach the agent; the first post into a channel with a canvas now returns that channel's brief instead of sending, and the brief can only narrow what gets said, never widen it, so a channel can't be used to smuggle out more than the origin channel intended to share. _Technical: preflight on `post_to_channel`, gated behind the mandate/mute checks and tracked per task so it survives respawns; canvases in the standing context block now show which channel(s) they're pinned in. PR #258._
- **Plugin agents — the non-engineering specialists like release-manager or ops — now know they're actually allowed to write files in their own workspace.** The prompt told every one of them it was strictly read-only, when the code has always granted Write/Edit/Bash sandboxed to the workspace; a concrete case this week saw release-manager decline to fix a Crashlytics config file it was fully entitled to write. _Technical: prompt and five architecture docs corrected across four review rounds to state the real tool list and write boundary; sandbox enforcement itself (workspace-only writes, OS-level and `PreToolUse` guard) is unchanged — only the prose was wrong. PR #259._

## 2026-08-06

- **Pinning one Slack canvas brief across several channels no longer doubles it up in the prompt.** Pinning a canvas as a tab in multiple channels is the recommended way to keep a single team-wide brief in one place instead of copy-pasting it per channel, but each channel's store adopted the canvas independently, so a task linked to threads in more than one of those channels got the same brief appended twice — wasted context, no wrong behavior. _Technical: `buildChannelCanvasPromptSection` dedupes on `file_id` via a `Set`; multi-thread-per-channel was already covered by the existing `channelIds` set. PR #257._

## 2026-08-05

- **A repeated pattern of Archie posting into channels nobody asked it to, and ignoring "stop" — the kind of incident that turned one bug triage into two threads and two people telling it to stop on 2026-08-05 — is fixed.** Mute now blocks outbound posts, not just inbound routing, across every posting tool, closes the workarounds (a new thread, a different channel, a teammate posting on your behalf), and voids any "I'll report back" promise that used to pull Archie into posting again; posting into another channel now requires quoting the specific person who asked for it, with filler like "urgent" or "n/a" rejected. _Technical: `isThreadMuted` resolves mute state via `findTaskByThread` so it holds across tasks sharing a thread; `post_to_channel` matches on channel id and requires a `mandate` string, logged as an auditable decision; PM per-turn checklist gains explicit "am I posting outside this thread" and "was I told to stop" questions; 24 new tests. PR #254._
- **Every teammate agent — not just the PM — now receives the channel's project brief, closing the gap where a specialist could discover something worth escalating but had no way to know who to route it to.** The brief is injected once after all agent branches spawn, so none can miss it, and the PM and specialist prompts now state the same handling rules — the brief carries the operational weight of a loaded skill and binds every task in that channel. _Technical: injection point moved to a single post-branch location in `spawn.ts`; `agent-core.md` states handling rules for repo/plugin agents in the same terms as `pm-agent.md`; `fetch_slack_reference` remains PM-only, so specialists must still ask the PM to open a referenced file. PR #256._
- **Slack canvas project briefs now render correctly instead of silently dropping content.** @-mentions and #-channel tags that used to vanish or turn into bogus file references now resolve to real names, tables that used to reach the PM as raw HTML now convert properly (including mentions and files nested inside them), and renaming a canvas's visible tab label is now enough to have it picked up or dropped from context — with drops announced instead of silent. _Technical: mention id prefixes (U/W/C/G/S/F) anchored and dispatched through the shared mention resolver; GFM table conversion fixed by promoting row 1 to `<th>` since Slack canvases carry no header markup; canvas discovery matches tab label or document title; `getChannelCanvasTabs` returns `null` (not `[]`) on failure so a transient error can't read as "every canvas removed"; closing `</canvas>`/`</channel_project_context>` tags stripped from injected bodies. PR #253._
- _Technical: task-metadata lookups (webhook branch/PR routing, Slack thread resolution, status queries) go back to using `grep` instead of a per-file sequential read — 47ms down to ~11ms on the prod fleet — while keeping the shell-injection fix that motivated removing grep in the first place, by validating the search needle's form before it's ever passed to the shell. PR #255._

## 2026-08-04

- **A boot-time bug that could quietly cost a task two of its three agents, with no retry or alert, is fixed.** A hard kill left an orphaned git config lock behind, which made startup recovery fail to re-message every agent listed after the first failure — so a task could sit `in_progress` missing agents indefinitely, with PM waiting on reports that would never arrive. Found via boot-log review of a real incident on this day. _Technical: `configureGitIdentity` now drops a stale `.git/config.lock` before writing identity, with the delete confined to paths under the workdir root after CodeQL flagged the unlink as path-injection; `recoverTaskAgents` now recovers each agent independently with per-agent try/catch, so the existing `spawned === 0` PM fallback also covers "every spawn failed"; two new test files reproduce the exact incident shape and fail against the pre-fix code. PR #252._

## 2026-07-28

- **A silent security regression that let sandboxed agents reach any network host — live since 2026-06-13 — is fixed, and package installs (`npm`/`yarn`) work in edit-mode tasks for the first time.** Egress enforcement had quietly stopped being honored after a transitive SDK bump that carried no signal of a security change, so the sandbox's promised deny-all was actually allow-all; separately, package managers could never have completed an install regardless, since their caches and Yarn Berry's own proxy config pointed at unwritable or unreachable locations. Verified with a live check that drives a real sandboxed agent through four assertions rather than trusting config shape alone — it has already caught one real regression on its first run. _Technical: egress now enforced from the `managedSettings` policy tier via `allowManagedDomainsOnly`, honored regardless of permission mode; `failIfUnavailable: true` closes a silent unsandboxed-fallback path; package-manager caches and global folders redirected into each agent's own workspace; a `BASH_ENV` script maps the sandbox's per-session proxy onto Yarn Berry's own config keys; SDK pinned exactly instead of by caret; full suite 882 passing. PR #242._
- **PMs can now check a task's token usage and cost on demand, broken down per agent.** A new PM-only `get_task_usage` tool reports total tokens (always available) plus SDK-reported cost (when available), where previously that data was recorded per turn but never aggregated or surfaced. _Technical: tokens aggregated crash-safely across all session transcripts, deduped by message id and including nested subagents; cost persisted verbatim from SDK result events to an append-only `usage.jsonl` and summed per `query()` call — never estimated or computed from a price table; hardened against CodeQL-flagged path-injection with a strict `taskId` shape guard. PR #232._
- **Archie now works in Slack group DMs, not just 1:1 DMs and channels.** An @mention creates a task and Archie replies in-thread; once engaged, further replies in that thread route to the same task with no re-mention needed, while ambient messages are otherwise ignored — treating a group DM as channel-like rather than assuming every message is meant for Archie. Verified live in a real group DM, including edit-mode approval and an ownership handoff. _Technical: `mpim:history`/`mpim:read` scopes and the `message.mpim` event added to the Slack manifest; existing DM-specific logic already keyed strictly off the `D` channel-id prefix so no new branching was needed; routing filters extracted into unit-testable pure helpers. Requires re-importing the Slack manifest and reinstalling the app per workspace. PR #223 (closes #215)._
- **The CLI task list no longer freezes to a blank header or jumps back to the top whenever anything changes elsewhere on the instance.** Three interacting bugs in the refresh path — silent fetch failures, a page-loading assumption that left gaps, and abandoned in-flight requests — could wedge the list empty, and every refresh also reset the scroll position, making a long task list effectively unnavigable. _Technical: retry-on-failure for page fetches, gap-filling prefetch instead of assuming contiguous pages, a generation token to discard stale responses, and in-place revalidation that preserves scroll position and selection; new `ink-testing-library` harness with regression tests confirmed failing before the fix and passing after. PR #111._
- _Technical: dependency bumps — npm minor/patch group (Claude Agent SDK, Anthropic SDK, AWS Bedrock runtime client, MCP SDK, chrono-node, ink, react, tsx), GitHub Actions minor/patch group (checkout, CodeQL, `claude-code-action`, `docker/login-action`), and standalone major-version bumps for croner (9→10) and TypeScript (6→7). PRs #239, #238, #214, #213._
- _Technical: plugin-declared repos are now pulled in parallel on startup instead of one at a time, so boot time tracks the slowest single repo rather than the sum of all of them; failures now log a warning and let boot continue instead of crashing it. PR #112._

## 2026-07-27

- _Technical: dependency bumps pushed straight to `main` — npm minor/patch group (Claude Agent SDK, Anthropic SDK, AWS Bedrock runtime client, MCP SDK, chrono-node, ink, react, `@types/node`, tsx) and GitHub Actions minor/patch group (`actions/checkout`, CodeQL init/analyze, `claude-code-action`, `docker/login-action`)._

## 2026-07-24

- **Archie's Opus-tier agents — PM plus `archie`, `data-analyst`, `backend`, `infrastructure`, `mobile`, and `release-manager` — move to Claude Opus 5 on the next deploy.** The `opus` alias resolves through the Claude Agent SDK rather than a pinned model id, so the upgrade is a version bump, not a config change; the Slack footer's model label also now derives generically from whatever model id the SDK resolves, so a future model launch renders correctly with no code change. _Technical: bumped `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` to 0.3.219, confirmed against published tarballs as the first release mapping `opus` → `claude-opus-5`; `modelDisplayLabel` rewritten to parse family + version out of any Claude id instead of a hard-coded table; the resolved model is captured once at session `init` (`Task.recordResolvedModel`) since it's fixed for a session; `sonnet[1m]` agents (`growth-ops`, `ops`, generic default) are unaffected. PR #236._

## 2026-07-20

- _Technical: the local copy of Forge (`.claude/workflows/forge-*.js`, `.claude/skills/forge/`, `.claude/commands/forge.md`) is removed now that it's distributed as the `forge` plugin in the `sweatco-claude-marketplace` repo, a functional superset of what lived here — keeping both invited `/forge` command-palette collisions and silent drift between the copies; `.gitignore`'s now-dead workflow re-include is dropped and `docs/proposals/forge.md` points at the plugin as the implementation home. PR #227._

## 2026-07-19

- **Operators can now ask for a post-ship change to a Forge PR and have it go through the same verified machinery as the original run, instead of a conductor hand-editing the branch.** `/forge revise <request>` puts the operator's own words through implementation, a full QA pass, a docs delta, and a PR/plan-record refresh — and it works even if the original session is gone, reconstructing the run from the `docs/plans/` record. A QA failure after a revision is now an honest dead-end (a fresh revise with an amended request) rather than a resume option that silently replays the same cached failure. Forge's review mode also gained a scope-questions channel: a fourth grounding lens reads open issues/PRs and `docs/proposals/`/`docs/plans/` so "competently built but possibly premature" work gets evidence-backed questions for the operator instead of a flat verdict, and run reports now state loop outcomes in words so a clean pass reads as verified rather than suspiciously quiet. _Technical: `forge-implement` gained a request mode where the operator's request becomes sanctioned scope on the existing branch; `forge-revise` chains request-mode implement → QA → docs → ship-style PR/plan refresh; plan shape validated fail-fast before the committing implement stage; `fixes`/`request` mutually exclusive; child error results carry a stage tag; a phase-display bug leaving permanently empty progress boxes on `forge-run`/`forge-revise` was removed. PR #222._

## 2026-07-17

- **Slack messages no longer show broken raw-text user mentions like `<@U03RQQTK1C3:Mikhail Froimson>`.** Agents were taught one mention marker but sometimes drifted to Slack's own native format instead, and the outbound converter only recognized the taught form — so the drifted version reached Slack unconverted and rendered as literal text. Mentions now render correctly whichever bracket order the agent uses, and Archie's internal marker is flipped to match Slack's native shape so the drift stops happening at the source. _Technical: `restoreMentions` accepts both bracket orders; producers (inbound mention render, knowledge-log source attributions, thread rendering) switched to `<@ID:Name>`; every parser widened to accept both orders so historical `@<...>` logs keep working; PM and memory-extractor prompts updated to match; full suite 829/829. PR #218._
- **The daily changelog can no longer silently lose days.** Previously the automation only ever looked at yesterday, so a failed run or an outage meant that day's changes were gone from the log for good, and a multi-day gap could never be repaired — which is exactly what let the log sit stale for days while unrelated work accumulated on `main`. The scheduled run is now self-healing: it finds every undocumented day since the newest entry (bounded to 14 days back), drafts one dated entry per pending day, and splices each into its correct reverse-chronological slot, even out of order. _Technical: `changelog-insert.mjs` accepts multiple dated sections per run, validates each independently, and refuses duplicate dates; publish commit message becomes `add entries for A..B` for multi-day runs; stale `[Unreleased]` section removed and the auto-maintained notice made visible in the intro. PR #217._
- _Technical: a changelog commit's `skip ci` marker left `main`'s tip without a CI run or a published image after every changelog push, complicating deploys — the marker is dropped so changelog commits build and publish like any other push. PR #219._
- _Technical: named Forge workflow lookup is cwd-scoped and resolves nothing in multi-repo remote sessions, since their cwd is the repos' parent directory — `forge-run` and the conductor now always launch by `scriptPath` and thread `workflowsDir` through to child stages, closing a landmine where a full `/forge` run would otherwise have died at its first stage boundary. PR #220._

## 2026-07-16

## Before this log — the starting point

Where Archie HQ stood before the first dated entry (late May 2026) — the foundation everything above built on.

### Already in place

- **An AI employee you work with in Slack.** Delegate a task in a Slack thread (or the local CLI) and Archie gets it done, then reports back. To users it presents as a single assistant that writes as "I" — the multi-agent machinery underneath is never exposed. It is **non-proactive** (only acts in response to a Slack message or GitHub webhook, never on its own) and **interruptible** (tasks can be stopped, resumed, and recovered).

- **A team of agents, not one chatbot.** A **PM agent** (Opus) reads the request, loads the relevant skill, and delegates to specialist agents (Sonnet). A designated **task owner** coordinates the work — sequentially or in parallel — and synthesizes the result. Agents talk to each other peer-to-peer and write discoveries, decisions, and blockers to a shared **knowledge log** that every agent reads for context.

- **Plugin architecture — add a department, not a fork.** New domains and abilities are added by dropping a plugin directory into the plugins repo; the engine discovers and loads them at startup with no core code changes. A plugin can contribute repo agents, plugin agents, a PM overlay, agent skills, hooks, and MCP server bindings.

- **Repo agents for engineering work.** Agents bound to a GitHub repository work in isolated shared git clones. They are **read-only by default**; once a human approves **edit mode**, the agent gets a feature branch, commits, and opens and manages its own pull requests.

- **Plugin agents for every other domain.** Marketing, analytics, ops, support, research, and more — lightweight agents that get a workspace, skills, and any MCP tools you wire up, with no git infrastructure.

- **GitHub integration with a merge orchestrator.** A webhook-driven PR workflow routes reviews, comments, CI results, and pushes to the right task, and merges pull requests automatically once they're ready. Force pushes are disallowed and pushing is blocked from agent Bash.

- **Human approval gate for any change.** Agents cannot modify code until a human approves edit mode via Slack buttons — the read-only-to-edit transition is an explicit, auditable step.

- **OS-level sandbox with defense-in-depth.** Each agent runs under per-agent filesystem isolation (bubblewrap on Linux, sandbox-exec on macOS), a network deny-all from agent Bash, and tool denylists — so a misbehaving or prompt-injected agent stays contained.

- **Web research pipeline.** Multi-agent web research with structured output and prompt-injection defenses, bounded by per-task budgets.

- **Per-task isolation and recovery.** Every task is its own runtime with isolated message queues, task-scoped budgets (research requests, inter-agent messages, wall-clock timeout), and metadata plus the knowledge log persisted to disk. Tasks recover automatically after a restart.

- **Persistent memory (optional, behind `ARCHIE_MEMORY`).** A cross-task memory layer so agents "arrive informed" instead of starting cold each time — user preferences, a rolling activity index, per-task summaries, and a graph of entity pages for the systems and concepts the work keeps touching. Plain Markdown, no database, removable as a single unit.

- **Encrypted secrets and OAuth.** External integrations connect via an OAuth flow, with tokens stored in an encrypted vault validated by a master key at startup.

- **Runs without Slack or GitHub.** A bundled example plugin set and an interactive CLI make a fresh clone runnable with only an Anthropic API key; Slack and GitHub are optional integrations.

- **Deployment and CI.** Docker Compose for dev and prod, an image published to GitHub Container Registry on every `main` build, and CI that runs typecheck, build, and tests. _(Dependabot, the CodeQL scan, the Docker-in-GitHub-Actions build, and AGPL-3.0 open-sourcing all arrived during the window above.)_
